Lane description: +0x19138 set_reserved_fee_recipients::handler (9176 B), normalized-equal; only file changed: instructions/admin/set_reserved_fee_recipients.rs (cumulative with the fz-A-srf-r1 partial already measured size-equal: global_config bound right after remaining_accounts, `.try_into().map_err(|_| ErrorCode::AccountNotEnoughKeys).unwrap()`, `copy_from_slice(&recipients[1..])`, `.iter().take(LEN).enumerate()`). New in this win: the validation loop is a `while let Some((i, account)) = accounts.next()` over an iterator scoped in its own `{ ... }` block (instead of `for`). Mechanism (IR-proven): the last residual (one sret reload `ldxdw r6,[r10-0x3d8]` placed after the key-check Display::fmt call instead of before the jump to the common return, plus a consequent tail-merge jump) is decided by the LLVM block order of the error-exit join blocks: rustc creates LLVM blocks lazily in MIR RPO; `for` desugars to a None-first switch, so the post-loop code (event/emit exits) is codegened before the loop body and the outer StorageDead(rent, recipients) join is created before the loop-exit join. `while let` gives a Some-first switch (loop body codegened first) and the block keeps StorageDead(iter) in the loop-exit chain, so the outer join is created after the loop-exit join, which reproduces the original Greedy-RA split placement (pre-opt IR block-move experiments + clang -O3 gave plain diff 0 before the source change). No behavior change: same iteration (first 8 accounts, same index i), same checks, errors, error lines (require_gte! line 40, require_keys_neq! line 60) and events. Positioning devices: none (line-neutral: the new `{` and `}` lines replace two existing blank lines, so every line number is unchanged; no comment/doc lines added, no #[inline(always)], no file moves). Runtime suite not run by lane.
